name: Create PO - GR - Invoice
narrative: Procure-to-Pay (P2P) is the sequence a company follows from the moment it needs to buy goods to the moment its supplier is paid. It begins when a buyer creates a Purchase Order specifying the supplier, material, plant, quantity, and negotiated net price. Once the goods physically arrive, the warehouse posts a Goods Receipt against the PO, confirming the delivered quantity and creating a Material Document that updates inventory. Finally, Accounts Payable creates a Supplier Invoice referencing the same PO, performs a three-way match (Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, Invoice) to confirm quantities and amounts agree, simulates the posting to catch account-determination or tax errors up front, then posts it to trigger payment.

glossary.meaning: Purchase Order — the buyer's commitment to purchase specific goods from a supplier
Goods Receipt — the warehouse's confirmation that ordered goods physically arrived
Verifying the Purchase Order, Goods Receipt, and Supplier Invoice all agree on quantity/amount before payment is released
The storage location goods are received into for this plant
A dry-run posting check that previews the accounting entries an invoice would create, without actually posting it
The vendor being paid for the goods
The accounting/inventory record created when stock physically moves (e.g., at Goods Receipt)

checkpoints: Stage 1 — Create Purchase Order: write down the Purchase Order number the system assigns you; you'll need it for Stage 2 and Stage 3.
Stage 2 — Post Goods Receipt: write down your new Material Document number.
Stage 3 — Post Supplier Invoice: write down your new Supplier Invoice number, and confirm the 3-way match showed no unexplained variance before posting.

quiz.question: What does a 3-way match actually compare?
quiz.answer: The Purchase Order, the Goods Receipt, and the Supplier Invoice — confirming quantities and amounts agree across all three before payment.

quiz.question: Why post a Goods Receipt before the Supplier Invoice?
quiz.answer: The invoice's 3-way match needs a Goods Receipt to compare against; posting the invoice first would have nothing to match.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of "Simulate" before posting an invoice?
quiz.answer: It previews the accounting entries and surfaces account-determination or tax errors before you actually commit the posting.

quiz.question: True or False: entering a Delivered Quantity larger than the PO's open quantity is always silently accepted.
quiz.answer: False — the system either blocks the posting or raises an over-delivery warning, depending on configuration.
